title: The Geometric Reasoner: Manifold-Informed Latent Foresight Search for Long-Context Reasoning
claim: Our training-free method consistently beats all baselines across math and coding benchmarks, converting modest compute into robust coverage.
layout: 1 panel, grouped bar chart, 7 benchmarks split math/coding by dashed divider
description: A single wide grouped bar chart of AUC score (y-axis, 0 to 80) across seven benchmarks. Four are math: MATH500, AIME25, OlympiadBench and OmniMath. Three are coding: HumanEval, BigCodeBench and LiveCodeBench. A dashed vertical line separates the two groups. Brackets under the x-axis label them Math Capabilities and Coding Capabilities. Each group has five bars: TGR-Latent in purple with diagonal hatching, Base Model in gray, PSampling in green, LCoT-SimKO in orange, and Dele-GRPO in pink. A legend runs along the top. Numeric values sit above every bar, and the TGR-Latent values are bold. The hatched purple bar is the tallest in nearly every group. Its lead over the gray base model is large, for example 71.5 against 57.1 on MATH500. The eye goes first to the hatched purple bars on the left of each cluster.
caption: TGR-Latent consistently outperforms baselines on Qwen3-8B. Manifold-informed latent foresight search steering converts modest inference-time compute into robust coverage without weight updates.
abstract: Scaling test-time compute enhances long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, yet existing approaches face a fundamental trade-off between computational cost and coverage quality: either incurring high training expense or yielding redundant trajectories. We introduce The Geometric Reasoner (TGR), a training-free framework that performs manifold-informed latent foresight search under strict memory bounds. At each chunk boundary, TGR scores candidate latent anchors via a lightweight look-ahead estimate combined with soft geometric regularizers that encourage smooth trajectories and diverse exploration. Chunk-wise KV cache resets keep memory linear in chunk length. On challenging math and code benchmarks, TGR improves robust trajectory coverage, measured by the area under the Pass@k curve (AUC), by up to 13 points on Qwen3-8B, with negligible overhead of about 1.1--1.3 times.
